_what: Every episode of profile 'prefix_dyn' over experiments/scenarios.yaml, scored with guardrail.kpi.compute - the same function the delivered flights use.
_not_kpi_grade: headless-kinematic topology, measured sim_speedup >> 1: functional evidence, never a contractual KPI number

_scope.grant_scope: not a grant row: the Prefix A/B (prefix on / off, same seed) on three dynamic template cells, generation N's CSP at the pilot
_scope.cadence: on demand (WP4-19, the four components on the grant's dynamic templates)
_scope.grant_sim_speedup: 1.0 on the hil rail - NOT met headless (measured speedup >> 1)
_scope.kpi_bearing_this_run_why: headless-kinematic topology, measured sim_speedup >> 1: no episode can be KPI-grade (guardrail.manifest.is_kpi_grade)

_distinct_kpi_signatures.note: episodes whose KPI tables differ (status, escapes, repairs, breaches, fail-safe, outcome, goal, time to safe, true-state distance and ticks, speed, range, offset). An upper bound on behavioural variety: float jitter in repair counts splits symmetric copies

_seeds.note: a deterministic episode repeated on another seed is identical by construction, not spread

warnings: every episode expects a fail-safe: a Shield that triggers on every episode scores the same as this one, so the target is not judged (meets_target None)

_failsafe_labels.observed_as: the escalation FSM entering RTL or Land (Shield.filter's FSM; a Brake or a Loiter is not a fail-safe trigger)

_arms.note: plumbing check only: every headless pilot ignores text, so the arms are the same flight by construction and any difference would be a harness defect. A robustness number needs a pilot that reads language.

aa.why: no A/A pair (prefix on flown twice on one seed) was flown, so there is no noise floor to read the delta against

prefix_consumer.labels_not_applied_to_prefix_on: the cell's outcome and fail-safe labels were derived for its rule-ignorant pilot; this is the prefix-on arm of a pilot that consumes the CSP, so they are not applied (its gates are)
prefix_consumer.note: the pilot is guardrail/prefix_consumer.py PrefixConsumer, the grant's default action-set adapter around the cell's own pilot law: a hand-written adapter, not a learned VLA. It reads the CSP's ranges, altitude band and forbidden polygons - the ones the Shield enforces - so part of the on / off delta holds by construction. The one A/B flown by a learned VLA reading the CSP as text (OpenVLA-7B, 7 Nov 2026, AirSimNH, outside this harness and not KPI-grade) is docs/data/csp_flights_20261107.json, and there the CSP did not help. Flown, CSP on against off over 3 seeds: mission success 0/3 on against 3/3 off (every prefix-on flight failed with unsafe_position_entered), repair rate on minus off mean +0.2006. Replayed open loop on the flights' own frames (14 runs, not flown): repair rate CSP minus off mean +0.0973, and CSP minus a rule-free neutral prefix of its length mean -0.0319, so the CSP's effect was not above the neutral prefix's

_true_state.basis: true position, harness oracle Shield; the grant's KPI is the Shield's own count (p0_escape_rate), reported unchanged. The autopilot_* figures are the modelled LOITER / RTL / LAND's, outside the Shield's escape rate by definition

results.why: The grant's worked example, as far as the Shield can take it: a polygon no-fly zone hot-applied mid-flight (Shield.hot_apply, generation 0 -> 1), its near edge `ahead_m` in front of the aircraft on its current heading. 3 m ahead leaves 2 m to the margin ring, so the reaction has to be immediate. At the grant's 5 s forecast (2026-10-12) every spawn but 30 m is inside the lookahead at 4 m/s (20 m), and 30 m is inside it at 8 m/s (40 m); at the 3 s forecast flown until then only 3 m (and 6 m at 4 m/s) were. The purpose holds: a zone appearing inside the forecast must be answered on the spawn tick. The zone never moves (dyn-nfz-translate below is the moving version), so the goal behind it is not reached, and no outcome is labelled.
results.labels_not_applied: the cell's outcome and fail-safe labels were derived for its rule-ignorant pilot; this is the prefix-on arm of a pilot that consumes the CSP, so they are not applied (its gates are)

corridor-drift-out's pilot (aimed straight out of the side at `ask_mps`) with the corridor narrowed mid-flight: at 3 s the 40 m route is swapped for one 10 m wide on the same centreline. Before the swap the old half-width (20 m) binds; after it the aircraft must be brought back inside 5 m and held there against a pilot still pulling out.
WHY ITS LABEL ACCEPTS P0 TICKS UNDER THE AUTOPILOT (2026-11-02): the Loiter timeout's RTL (rubric E5) flies the straight leg home, its forecast crossing the narrowed corridor's wall on 4-8 RTL ticks; it ends inside the corridor.

A 20 x 20 m zone across the route; the Shield holds the aircraft where its 5 s forecast just clears the margin ring (19.6 m short of it at 4 m/s, measured at 9.9 s). At 10 s the zone grows by `factor` about its centre, so its ring now covers where the aircraft waits: legal one tick, inside the ring the next through no move of its own (imposed, not a breach). It must get out, and not fly back in. The growth is small enough that the escape at GeofenceEscape's 2 m/s takes under the escalation FSM's T = 5 s (3.3: 3.2 m into the ring, out in 1.7 s; 3.8: 8.2 m, out in 4.2 s), so no fail-safe is expected. RE-CUT 2026-10-12 for the grant's 5 s forecast. Written for the 3 s forecast, the aircraft waited 11.6 m short of the ring and the factors were 2.5 and 3.0; at 5 s it waits 19.6 m short, so 2.5 no longer reached it (no time to safe: the cell's purpose gone, its gate failing) and 3.0 reached 0.2 m. The factors now put the ring the same 3.2 and 8.2 m past the aircraft as before, and the start moved from x -60 to -75 so the launch point stays outside the grown zones (radius-scaling-grow-deep too).
